So the mechanic is: clicking the ring (target) makes the nearest object on the line move to the ring? The diamond was the first object on the line (closest to the ring? no, the diamond was farthest from the ring… actually the line goes diamond (36,7) → square (47,17) → cross (59,27). The ring is at (21,40), which is on the extension of the line beyond the diamond! Let me check: the line's direction from cross to square to diamond: from (59,27) to (47,17): -12 rows, -10 cols; from (47,17) to (36,7): -11, -10. Extending beyond the diamond: (36,7) - (11,10) ≈ (25,-3)… hmm, that would give col -3, not 40. So the ring isn't on the extension of the line.
Wait, actually the line from the diamond to the square: slope is roughly +1 row per col. The ring at (21,40) is upper-right of the diamond. Not on the line.
But the diamond moved to the ring. So clicking the ring teleports the diamond there. Or: the diamond is a "ball" and clicking the ring makes the ball travel… hmm.

Actually wait — maybe the line is a "rope" connecting the objects, and clicking the ring makes the object at the end of the rope (the diamond) move to the ring, shortening the rope. Now the rope connects ring-diamond → square → cross. Next, clicking the ring again might pull the square into the ring? Then the cross?
Goal: probably get the cross (or all objects) into the ring. Or maybe the goal is to get the diamond back? Hmm.
Let me look at the new frame more carefully: the diamond inside the ring — is it the same hash? Let me check the segmentation. Also check whether the line changed: previously the line ran from (36,7) through (47,17) to (59,27). Now the line runs from the ring (21,40) through the square to the cross. The line segment from the diamond to the square is now from the ring to the square — a different path. So the rope re-anchored: the diamond is now at the ring, and the rope connects ring → square → cross.
Hypothesis: the rope connects the three objects in order: A (diamond) - B (square) - C (cross). Clicking the ring moves object A to the ring. Then maybe clicking the ring again moves B? Or does the ring need to be clicked again?
Or maybe the goal is: the magenta center of the square is special; the ring is a "goal hole"; you need to get the cross into the ring? But the cross is at the far end.
Let me probe: click the ring center again and see if the square moves.
Actually, wait. Maybe the mechanic is different: clicking the ring makes the first object (the one closest to the ring along the rope?) move to the ring. The diamond was closest to the ring?
